author: Greg Pickel
title: Everything Penn State coach Matt Campbell said following the Lions' 24-20 loss to Wisconsin - NewsBreak
text:
By Greg Pickel ,
7 hours ago
Sep 26, 2026; University Park, Pennsylvania, USA; Penn State Nittany Lions head coach Matt Campbell looks on during a warmup prior to the game against the Wisconsin Badgers at West Shore Home Field at Beaver Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Matthew O'Haren-Imagn Images STATE COLLEGE — Penn State coach Matt Campbell discussed his team’s struggles in offense, Wisconsin’s game-winning touchdown, and more after the Lions’ 24-20 loss to Wisconsin. The first question he fielded focused on the Lions’ inability to move the ball consistently during the game.
“We really struggled to find the rhythm,” Campbell said. “I think in the first half, you were either backed up or you were on the goal line, and so kind of never got into the flow of the game. I feel like it kind of led to the second half of the football game and kind of being in the same spot where we just struggled. And, I think we had a lot of play opportunities to be made, and we just didn’t make some plays that we had the opportunity to.”
You can watch Campbell’s full news conference here . You can read everything he said below.
On the Penn State defense in the fourth quarter and the Wisconsin game-winning touchdown Campbell: I think we had a guy slip on the broken play. One slip and, again, that play, that situation is kind of the narrative of the second half. We left it to chance. And we had so many opportunities to put the game away, and we just didn’t take advantage of those opportunities. And so, obviously, that play will stick out. But the reality of it is, you know, defensively, I thought we played a tremendous football game. We gave ourselves every opportunity to win the football game, and we didn’t take advantage of it as a team when we had the opportunity to do that.
Q: On the decision before the end of the half to not push for points and not going for it on 4th and 1 to start the fourth quarter Campbell: I forget what happened on the first play. I don’t know if it was a penalty or whatever that was, and then my concern a little bit was that. We can put some judgment on the head coach right there. The third, fourth, and one, should we go for it? Should we not? I felt like we were playing such good defense there that I just didn’t want to put our team at risk. That’ll eat at me. The other thing is they had two timeouts, and I didn’t want to give them the ball back there either at the end of the half. When it started negative, I just felt like the biggest thing for us is, let’s get this thing into halftime. Let’s make the corrections, knowing that we had a really significant lead at the point. We can come out, play great defense, get the football back and kind of take the game over.
Q: What do you say about the performance you got from [Penn State QB] Rocco Becht tonight, and obviously the pick there to start the second half? Campbell: I think Rocco… It’ll be interesting to answer that question probably a little bit better after watching the videotape. But I thought Rocco made some tremendous plays. I thought he kept us in the football game; Some scrambles that were timely, some scrambles and throws. Felt like some of our issues were probably more so with some protection things, where even that ball was tipped. It wasn’t a ball that was like a bad or poor decision. It was a tipped pass. So I really thought Rocco played, I thought, a really good football game for the most part. Again, I’ll answer that better after I watch the video tonight.
Q: Did you feel like not having Koby (Howard) had any role in the offense’ inability to sustain rhythm, or is it just an inability to stay in rhythm period? Campbell: I think the one thing Koby has done a great job of is, he’s made great plays. He’s had the ability to make some of those plays that were available, and he’s made some of those plays. I would be a fool to sit up here and say we didn’t miss Koby. But I would also say I have great belief in the rest of our guys. The rest of our guys had some opportunities, and they’ve gotta continue to pound away at it. Koby’s a guy that we all have great faith in, and we’re certainly really proud of.
Q: Your staff and your players expressed a lot of confidence in the receiver group beyond Koby today. Chase [Sowell] was the only guy who had a reception from that receiver unit. What was the ultimate breakdown, and why were you not able to get more guys involved and get them touches? Were you surprised at all by the end result of the stat sheet? Campbell: I would say that I am a little bit surprised. I would say I’m a little bit surprised that is the statistic in the game. There was just a weird flow to the game, a little bit, and especially in the first half of the football game, where we’re playing situational football. Where I think some of it will be really interesting, what happened in the second half? I think I’ll have a better answer for you guys on Tuesday to that question. But obviously, we’re going to have to have more production from the receiving room, from the other players on the offensive side of the ball. That won’t cut it [with] what it looked like tonight.
Q: Matt, not getting a touchdown early and having to settle for the field goal. What effect did that have, and also, up 17-0, how did the Wisconsin’s touchdown before the half change things? Campbell: I’d say the first three games we did a great job in the middle eight. And I think today we lose the middle eight 6-0 right? They had the opportunity to put points on the board right before half, and they get the opportunity to do it coming out. I think from our end of it, that was a great opportunity up 17, to really give ourselves a great momentum going forward. We didn’t have any opportunity to score points there, and obviously we didn’t score the rest of the game.
I think that first possession, it was a little bit goofy down there, too. I think the penalty that happened kind of got goofy in terms of what we saw, it was a different defense than maybe what we had prepared for. I thought we did a great job after the first preparation. We got down there, we made the right adjustments, and I thought had the right play calls in terms of what we wanted to do. But I think that’s going to happen early in a football game. You’ve got to make adjustments based on what those guys do, and I thought our staff did do a really good job of that, the second two times we got down there.
Q: Matt, just your thoughts on the Penn State running game. It looked like James Peoples was actually your most productive back today. What do you think of the rotation, and do you think you would be able to get more out of it, even though you didn’t have Koby available at that stretch of the end? Campbell: I would say first of all, I thought James ran the ball really well today. I thought he made some really key plays in some key situations. I do. I thought the running game, again, offensively, it was choppy. I wish I could tell you it was better. You guys, I think, all know that, you’ve seen us play. That’s not the rhythm that we want to play in, and we’re going to have to be better. But I think it was choppy all around, with the running backs, the receivers, the O-line; there’s got to be a significant improvement to be the team we need to be.
Q: Coach, all losses are difficult. The way that you guys lost this one, and just being the Big Ten opener, you got a short week. You got to go on the road to prepare. What’d you tell the guys, and what did some of the leaders say to the guys in the locker room on how to handle this one and move forward? Campbell: I know I’ve said this multiple times: Adversity is what college football is about. The ability to overcome adversity and the ability to unify and rally forward. This will be a great test for us. We’re going to find out a lot more about ourselves here in the next six days, from our coaching staff and our players. The reality of it is that these are all correctable things, if we’re willing and humble enough to be able to make the great corrections. So it will be a great challenge for us. It’s not going to be easy, but we look forward to the challenge to grow ourselves forward.
